data.one_liner: Add real-time chat and messaging features to your Flutter application using the Sendbird backend.
data.what_it_does: Provides APIs to connect to the Sendbird chat service, manage open and group channels, send various message types (text, files, multiple files), and handle real-time chat events. It also handles local caching of chat data using Isar.
use_when: You need a fully managed, scalable chat and messaging solution backed by Sendbird.
You want real-time messaging, channel management, and offline message caching in your app.
avoid_when: You want to host your own chat backend without relying on a third-party hosted service like Sendbird.
You only need local database storage without any server-side chat functionality.
strengths: Feature-rich chat solution supporting open channels, group channels, and file messages.
Built-in offline support and local data caching via Isar.
Cross-platform support across mobile and web.
weaknesses: Relies entirely on a proprietary hosted backend service.
Requires minimum platform versions such as Android minSdkVersion 23 or higher.
data.setup_notes: Requires creating a Sendbird application on the Sendbird Dashboard to obtain an App ID. Also requires setting the minimum SDK version on Android to 23 or higher and adding Apple privacy manifests on iOS if required.

alternatives.name: intercom_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose Intercom if your primary goal is customer support messaging and user engagement rather than custom in-app chat.

alternatives.name: onesignal_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose OneSignal if you are strictly looking for push notifications and messaging campaigns rather than a complete real-time chat SDK.
